items.title: Flinders Island bushfire grows to 13,000 hectares with Tasmanian homes and properties at risk
items.summary:
Fire making a ‘significant run’ towards the southwest of the island on Thursday, Tasmania Fire Service says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Homes and properties on a picturesque remote island remain under threat from an out-of-control bushfire that has sent smoke hundreds of kilometres south.

The blaze on Flinders Island in Bass Strait spread significantly on Wednesday after being started by lightning strikes.

Continue reading...
items.t: Large bushfire threatens homes and properties on remote island off Tasmania

items.title: Australian politics live: Hanson ‘delighted’ as Liberal senator defects to One Nation; Bowen says global tensions ‘infected’ Cop31
items.summary:
• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson has released a statement this morning welcoming South Australian senator Leah Blyth to her party.

Blyth is the second high-profile federal defection from the Coalition to One Nation – after Barnaby Joyce.

Senator Blyth will be One Nation’s first South Australian Senator and will build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state.

My team and I are delighted to welcome Senator Blyth to sit in the Senate with One Nation.

We are facing at the next election clearly a coalition of the Liberals, Nationals and One Nation, with all the baggage that each of these parties brings to the table. They’re all anti-worker, they’re all extreme … this demonstrates, I think, more disunity in the Liberal party under Angus Taylor.
items.t: Australian politics live: Canavan calls Blyth a ‘turncoat’ after One Nation defection; Bowen says forces ‘infected’ Cop31

items.title: Liberal senator Leah Blyth announces defection to One Nation
items.summary:
South Australian senator labels One Nation the ‘only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around’

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, has announced she is defecting to One Nation, becoming the party’s first upper-house member for the state.

Blyth, a member of Angus Taylor’s frontbench, said she did not believe the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government, which was “running the country into the ground”.

items.t: Liberal senator Leah Blyth announces defection to One Nation

items.title: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?
items.summary: Just days after its release, Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a vehicle for political misinformation. Viral footage falsely claims the game features a mission recreating Charlie Kirk’s assassination, while pro-Russian accounts are sharing fake screenshots containing anti-Ukrainian messages. Meanwhile, Russia’s own Defence Ministry has exploited the game's popularity to promote military recruitment. Vedika Bahl explains how GTA 6 is being used to push real political agendas in Truth or Fake.
items.t: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?

items.title: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war
items.summary: Russian government data obtained by pro-Ukraine hackers and analyzed by the BBC indicates that Russia has lost at least 490,334 soldiers during its war on Ukraine.
items.t: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.summary:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...
items.t: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, says president

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments

items.title: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators
items.summary: Ever since 1965 when the French first got to cast a ballot by universal suffrage for their president, they've valued campaign rules that guarantee ‘equal time’ for candidates. But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week a bombshell announcement ahead of next Spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced air time rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period. Here at France 24, we’re already testing the stopwatches and combing ove the guest list spreadsheets. Should podcasters, YouTubers and influencers be subjected to the same rules as us?
items.t: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators

items.title: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs
items.summary: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
items.t: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs

items.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, target of Trump’s immigration crackdown, lands in Spain after ‘leaving happy’
items.summary:
Ábrego García chooses to depart from US after previously being deported to El Salvador due to ‘administrative error’

  • US politics – live updates

Kilmar Ábrego García, the Salvadorian national whose mistaken deportation turned him into a symbol of Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts, has landed in Spain.

Ábrego García arrived in Madrid on Wednesday after leaving the United States of his own volition.

Continue reading...
items.t: Kilmar Ábrego García, target of Trump’s immigration crackdown, lands in Spain after ‘leaving happy’

items.title: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges
items.summary: Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery. The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.
items.t: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges

items.title: Poland says will create no-fly zone at Ukraine border after repeated airspace violations
items.summary: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods. The no-fly zone is intended to allow Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.
items.t: Poland says will create no-fly zone at Ukraine border after repeated airspace violations

items.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
items.summary: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production -- the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The duties, proposed at up to 20 percent, come over allegations the economies "are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles," a senior US official said on condition of anonymity. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight.
items.t: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China

items.title: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
items.summary: Iran's U.N. envoy claims the U.S. military used Palantir and Anthropic AI systems to select some 2,000 targets over just four days.
items.t: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI during war

items.title: The ‘French Milei’? Presidential candidate David Lisnard aims to reshape France’s right wing
items.summary: Having secured reelection victory Wednesday as leader of France's mayors, Cannes Mayor David Lisnard turns once more to build on his recent bid for the Élysée. As his Nouvelle Énergie movement gains momentum, questions swirl over whether his campaign will reshape the French political landscape, or if his party will ultimately cosy up to the far right ahead of France’s 2027 race to the polls.
items.t: The ‘French Milei’? Presidential candidate David Lisnard aims to reshape France’s right wing

items.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
items.summary: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.
items.t: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era

items.title: EU nationals will pay higher tuition fees than UK students, Burnham indicates
items.summary:
Asked by Kemi Badenoch to rule out equal rate for UK and EU students, PM says proposal ‘will not be put on the table’

European students will have to pay higher fees than their domestic equivalents at UK universities under a still-to-be-finalised part of the new deal with the EU, Andy Burnham has indicated.

The issue of fees paid by EU nationals studying at British universities is the main element of the arrangement hailed by Burnham in Brussels on Friday that has not been agreed, with both sides giving an extra six months to reach a solution.

Continue reading...
items.t: EU nationals will pay higher tuition fees than UK students, Burnham indicates

items.title: Titanic postcard sent days before doomed voyage sells for pricey sum
items.summary: A postcard from Jack Phillips, the Titanic's chief radio officer, was postmarked April 6, 1912, four days before the ill-fated ship set sail.
items.t: Titanic postcard sent days before doomed voyage sells for pricey sum

items.title: Turkey's deadly factory blast: 'Investing in safety costs more than letting people die'
items.summary: An explosion at a steel factory on November 9 in Turkey's Aliaga, near Izmir, killed 19 people. This tragedy follows several others and highlights the issues surrounding workers’ safety in Turkey, our Observers say. They also condemn the repressive responses from the government and the company.
items.t: Turkey's deadly factory blast: 'Investing in safety costs more than letting people die'

items.title: Serbia government wants to limit reality TV, adopt 4-day work week
items.summary: Serbia's Student List party, which recently ousted the country's Russia-aligned strongman leader, wants to restrict reality TV.
items.t: Serbia government wants to limit reality TV, adopt 4-day work week

items.title: Paris takes on masculinist movements
items.summary: As masculinist movements face their first major trial in Paris, the city has announced several initiatives to combat this ideology. The campaign aims to call attention to the real-world danger posed by misogynist groups online. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler takes a closer look.
items.t: Paris takes on masculinist movements

items.title: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline
items.summary: As France's mayors gather in Paris for their annual convention, the decline in living standards and public services in both urban and rural areas is high on the agenda. Rural mayors, in particular, are concerned about the shrinking populations of their communities. But one small French town bucking the trend is Parlan, in the Cantal region, where the population has doubled and local services have flourished thanks to an offer of virtually free plots of land.
items.t: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline

items.title: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions
items.summary: Moldova is urging its citizens to prepare for emergencies as the war in neighbouring Ukraine brings new risks across its border. The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.
items.t: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions

items.title: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
items.summary: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.
items.t: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader

items.title: Huang's return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
items.summary: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. After vaulting more than 30 percent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback, Nvidia fell almost six percent Tuesday. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
items.t: Huang's return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop

items.title: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison
items.summary: Twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are awaiting their sentences in Iran. They were arrested in January 2026, at the age of just 19, for taking part in protests against the Iranian regime. Taraneh is facing the death penalty, while Romina has been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Their family has been campaigning for their release.
items.t: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison

items.title: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – as it happened
items.summary:
German chancellor, in wide-ranging speech, says Moscow is ‘escalating on a massive scale’

If you want to hear more about the new death toll, listen to today’s Today in Focus podcast with our Russia expert, Pjotr Sauer.

“Two groups of hackers accessed Russia’s main statistics database last month and discovered a cache of 11m death certificates that revealed nearly 500,000 Russian losses in Ukraine since 2022. Among these were 1,000 – the equivalent of a whole regiment – who took their own lives.

The documents show how the majority of soldiers come from poorer areas and ethnic minorities, drawn in by high salaries. There are also recruits from abroad and even those lured to Russia by offers of jobs. But for how long can Vladimir Putin keep this shocking death toll from the Russian people?”

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – Europe live

items.title: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
items.summary: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.
items.t: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000

items.title: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives
items.summary: An enormous explosion rang out across rural Iowa Tuesday as the US military carried out the controlled detonation of some 10,000 pounds of lead azide. US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion. But the risk of a toxic cloud of lead dust spreading out from the blast zone has caused public safety fears among locals.
items.t: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives

items.title: Colombia: Security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege
items.summary: Some 25 people being held hostage by gunmen in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, were freed Tuesday after security forces stormed the building. One assailant was killed during the operation but no hostages were injured.
items.t: Colombia: Security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege

items.title: US Army detonates lead explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
items.summary: The US Army on Wednesday blew up 5 tons of lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in Iowa despite community backlash over fears of environmental contamination. The detonation was postponed three times, but got the green light after a federal appeals court this week found the US Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards to minimise the dispersal of lead dust.
items.t: US Army detonates lead explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears

items.title: High-quality medieval armor discovered in shipwreck that sank in 1495
items.summary: The ship, known as "Griffin" or "Gribshunden," was the warship of Denmark's 15th-century leader King Hans.

items.title: 'We need to stop the war in Iran': US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal
items.summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Democratic Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal laid out her priorities for the new Congress: ending the war in Iran, tackling the cost-of-living crisis, curbing political corruption and holding the Trump administration accountable for its immigration crackdown. She also called for the "complete" dismantling of the US federal immigration agency ICE and backed an end to US military funding for Israel.
items.t: 'We need to stop the war in Iran': US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal

items.title: Brussels on split-screen: where it flexes – and where it bends
items.summary:
From a choreographed summit that dominated Westminster but barely registered in Brussels to a climate showdown in Turkey, last week revealed the EU’s priorities – and the limits of its collective power

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Two very different European diplomatic dramas played out almost simultaneously last week. On Friday, a tightly choreographed EU-UK summit transfixed London, while barely registering on the continent. On Sunday, Cop31 collapsed after a united EU forcefully vetoed a watered-down climate pact, even as it relaxed its own green rules at home.

What do these two events reveal about the EU: how it works, what takes up its bandwidth, how it exercises its clout – and where it’s vulnerable?

***

items.t: Brussels on split-screen: where it flexes – and where it bends

items.title: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
items.summary: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?
items.t: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation

items.title: Brits are having less sex, but watching a lot of porn, survey finds
items.summary: A third of Brits aged 16 to 24 have never had sex, a landmark survey finds, though most acknowledge sexting and watching pornography.
items.t: Brits are having less sex, but watching a lot of porn, survey finds

items.title: Libya’s Haftar visits old foe Turkey for first time in ‘new phase’ of ties
items.summary: Eastern Libya military commander Khalifa Haftar met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Wednesday during his first official visit to Turkey, marking a major thaw in relations between the longtime rivals. The visit came days after Ukraine struck a Russian warship in Benghazi, a port city controlled by Haftar.
items.t: Libya’s Haftar visits old foe Turkey for first time in ‘new phase’ of ties

items.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".
items.t: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war

items.title: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president
items.summary: The Mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard, has been re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, securing a comfortable victory in a vote announced on Wednesday. Lisnard is also a candidate in next year's French presidential election. For more on what his re-election could mean, FRANCE 24's James André reports from the Association of Mayors' convention in Paris.
items.t: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president

items.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.
items.t: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
items.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Continue reading...
items.t: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations

items.summary:
The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

items.title: Aidan is one of thousands of students forced to verbally defend his honours thesis as universities take on AI
items.summary:
Honours students are increasingly being asked to sit oral assessments – but at the University of Sydney it’s become a requirement for all

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When Aidan Elwig Pollock signed up for an honours program at the University of Sydney, he did not expect his 20,000-word thesis to be accompanied by a spoken component.

But, as AI increasingly makes written research an unreliable form of assessment, the university has demanded all students taking the one-year program defend their arguments in conversation with professors.

items.title: Number of women killed by men in Ireland almost doubles in a year
items.summary:
Figures from past 30 years show more than half of victims killed by current or ex-partner

The number of women in Ireland killed by men has surged in the past five years and risen especially sharply in the past 12 months, according to a study.

After falling for two decades, the number of violent deaths began going up in 2021 and has risen sharply this year, with 13 deaths so far, the report by Irish charity Women’s Aid said on Wednesday.

Social media campaign fronted by British rapper Shao Dow advises tourists not to let their guard down

The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital.

In a recent clip made in conjunction with the embassy, the British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, a frequent visitor to Japan, notes that although the country “is incredibly safe, that doesn’t mean you can let your guard down”.

items.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol.

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour

Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

items.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
items.summary:
Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran

Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view.

Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geostrategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race.

Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.

Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.
